subject: Request: VPC Latency Liability Variance — Peregrine Private Deployment
summary: Customer requests a limited SLA variance for latency attribution on a private VPC where transit peering and egress are customer-controlled. Sales to validate operational impact and legal to propose narrow language that limits Redwood liability and preserves fallbacks.
messages:
From: Janelle Cruz <janelle.cruz@peregrine-sys.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@peregrine-sys.com, legal.ops@peregrine-sys.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VPC latency liability variance for private deployment

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team reviewed Redwood Private in the staging VPC and we need to formalize an exception to the standard latency SLA for the production deployment.

Background: Peregrine controls the transit peering and egress points for the colo where Redwood will be deployed. We observed occasional 250-500ms tail latencies during peak WAN bursts that are out of our (and your) control. We still want Redwood to meet availability SLOs for control-plane and KV caching, but we need an explicit allocation of responsibility for network-induced token latency so we can retain our internal SLAs to downstream customers.

Request: a narrow, time-boxed variance that: 1) excludes customer-controlled transit and last-mile peering from per-request latency calculations; 2) defines evidence rules (packet captures, traceroutes, sampling windows) that both parties will accept; and 3) a fallback path/rollover obligation for Redwood if sustained tail latency persists beyond agreed thresholds.

Attached: network diagram (peregrine_network_diagram_v2.pdf) and sample latency dumps (latency-samples-march-2028.csv).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept a limited liability variance and what evidence you would need?

Best,
Janelle Cruz
Head of Cloud Architecture
Peregrine Systems

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Cruz <janelle.cruz@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VPC latency liability variance for private deployment

Janelle —

Appreciate the clear ask and the artifacts. Short answer: yes, we can discuss a narrow variance, but we need to operationalize it so it doesn't become an SLA hole for other customers and to protect Redwood's uptime guarantees. Proposed next steps from our side: 

- Vivek (solutions) to outline technical evidence and acceptable sampling cadence for attributing token latency to Peregrine-controlled transit.
- Kim (legal) to draft a tightly-scoped clause that excludes customer-controlled network egress/peering from per-token latency SLOs when validated by evidence, while preserving availability and failover obligations on Redwood.
- Align on a 30‑day pilot window in staging to validate detection heuristics and fallback timing.

Can we set up a 45-minute call Monday to agree on evidence and pilot metrics? I’ll loop Vivek and Kim into that invite.

Thanks,
Michael
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0127

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, Janelle Cruz <janelle.cruz@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VPC latency liability variance for private deployment

Thanks — adding a technical note before the call so we can align quickly.

Operational evidence we typically accept: 
- Synchronized traceroute windows from both sides showing queuing at an intermediate ASN with timestamps aligned to request IDs.
- TCP/UDP packet captures (pcap) for the sampled requests with matching request/response IDs and MSL timestamps.
- Agent-side metrics: egress queue depth, retransmit counts, and WAN burst indicators for sampled 1-minute windows.

Suggested detection heuristic for the pilot: when 95th/99th token-latency exceeds SLA by >200ms and external traceroute indicates hop beyond Peregrine boundary with matching queuing indicators, mark event as "customer-network" for that interval. During the 30-day pilot we will: 1) run continuous sampling on a 10% traffic subset, 2) produce a daily evidence bundle, and 3) trigger automated rollover to an alternate region if sustained for >15 minutes and impacting >1% of requests.

We will need access to the packet captures you attached and permission to run a short traceroute agent from the colo egress to Redwood ingress for a 72-hour window during the pilot. If Peregrine approves data-sharing, our SREs can correlate.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, Janelle Cruz <janelle.cruz@peregrine-sys.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VPC latency liability variance for private deployment

Hi all — following our call this morning, attaching the draft language we discussed (proposed-sla-variance-draft.docx). Key points in plain language: 

1) Scope: The variance applies only to per-request token-latency targets for private deployments where customer-managed transit/peering is in use and where evidence (as defined) demonstrates network causation. It does not affect Redwood availability or control-plane SLOs.
2) Evidence Rules: Both parties must provide synchronized traceroutes and packet captures for any disputed incident; Redwood reserves the right to jointly-validate with a mutually agreed third-party network forensics provider if necessary.
3) Duration & Review: Initial variance is time-boxed to 12 months with quarterly review; either party may terminate the variance with 30 days' notice if operational risk increases.
4) Fallback: If customer-network attribution is inconclusive and sustained latency exceeds the agreed threshold for >15 minutes and impacts >1% of requests, Redwood will automatically fail-over traffic to an alternate region or model variant (subject to capacity) and will notify Peregrine within 5 minutes.

We tried to keep the language narrow — this is intentionally not a blanket carve-out. Please let me know any material concerns from Peregrine legal or ops and whether the evidence types below are acceptable.

Attachments: proposed-sla-variance-draft.docx

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
